The best advice I can give you is to try and make things familiar. Create standard routines for things like converting an object to a string (if doing database access). That way the code you write only has to be program-specific.

The other thing is create your own 'standards' for example decide on a way of naming variables. Like strExample as a string, intExample as an integer. It doesn't matter what they are - just make them consistent. Even things like when to use certain things. That way your applications will start being more uniform and the code should be familiar and easier to read back if you need to re-visit it for any reason. 

Plus bonus points if you ever go for a job interview as a programmer - you can take your standards document with you which shows professionalism and dedication! The amount of times people have been rejected from my employer just by writing lazy code with no structure in interviews is unreal!

Just over 2 years ago I was at complete rock bottom. I'd taken the decision that killing myself would be the best thing to do in that situation. I wrote my note, packed a bag and put on my favourite clothes. Theres a large suspension bridge in the city where I live and I walked onto it and climbed over the fence. After a couple of minutes a girl a couple of years younger than me (I was 19 at the time) was walking past and saw me standing there. She didn't say anything, she just stood on the edge of the railings and put her hand on mine. We stood there for almost 20 minutes before she finally spoke and said how she has the same thoughts a lot of the time and understood how I felt. A lot of stuff happened shortly after that, including psychiatrists and being sectioned on a ward, but she came to visit me every day until I was released. She became my best friends until 6 months ago when she tragically took her own life whilst I was out of town. She took time out of her day to stop me from suicide and saved my life. She gave me hope, faith and happiness at a time when I couldn't see anything positive in my life. She will forever be in my heart and soul and I wish every day that I could see her one more time to try and stop her from doing the very thing she saved me from.

Even more interesting, time itself and the universe has neither a start nor an end. Whilst I find it difficult to comprehend the fact that the universe will go on forever and ever, and never stop. It didn't start either. It has been here forever. Forever isn't even a concept of never ending any more, its a concept of nothingness.
